lines: Thursday, 14 May 2026
ARBITRATOR:  Good morning.  Any housekeeping before we start
with the witness?
MR LIXENBURG:  No, thank you.  Thank you for permitting us
to interpose Mr Viriot, and Ms Bejoy for accommodating
that.
Mr Khaled is outside the room for the moment whilst
Mr Viriot --
ARBITRATOR:  I asked him to go and enjoy his coffee out
there.
MR LIXENBURG:  Thank you.
MR HUBERT VIRIOT (called)
MR LIXENBURG:  Mr Viriot, there should be an affirmation in
front of you, I wonder if you could please read that.
WITNESS:  Sure.  I, Hubert Viriot, solemnly, sincerely, and
truly swear and affirm that the evidence I give shall be
the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.
Examination-in-chief by MR LIXENBURG
MR LIXENBURG:  Thank you very much.  If we could look at
{C2-1}.  I think you have a hard copy in front of you,
you can look at either.  Is that your first witness
statement?
A.  Yes.
Q.  If we could go to the last page 5, is that your
signature?
A.  Correct.
Q.  If we could look at {C5-1}, do you recognise that as
your second witness statement?
A.  Yes.
Q.  If we could go to the last page of that, page 8, is that
your signature?
A.  Correct.
Q.  Are those two witness statements true to the best of
your knowledge and belief?
A.  Absolutely.
MR LIXENBURG:  Thank you.  Ms Bejoy will have some
questions.
Cross-examination by MS BEJOY
ARBITRATOR:  Ms Bejoy, we know that the witness has a flight
to catch, so need to be on time for him.
MS BEJOY:  Sure, arbitrator.  Thank you.
Hi, Mr Hubert, how are you today?
A.  Very well, thank you.  Good morning.
Q.  Morning.  So I understand from your first witness
statement that you are currently the vice-chairman of
Yotel Limited, correct?
A.  That's in my second witness statement, yes.
Q.  Okay.
A.  I have changed.  I used to be the CEO back in the first
statement.
Q.  Could you please confirm whether Yotel Limited is the
parent or a holding company of the Yotel brand?
A.  Absolutely.  Yotel Investment Ltd is the owner of Yotel
brand co, which holds the IP of Yotel.
Q.  Could you please confirm since when you are associated
with Yotel Limited?
A.  Since the -- trying to be exactly precise, May 2014.
Q.  Okay.  I saw a reference to two names, Yotel Limited and
Yotel Investments Limited.  Are they the same?
A.  No, Yotel Investments Limited is the holding company of
Yotel Limited.  It is purely an investment vehicle which
owns the company.
Q.  What is the relationship between Yotel Limited and IFA
Yotel Investment FZE?
A.  IFA Yotel resort, there is none -- legally?
Q.  Yes, are you aware of any relationship or connection?
A.  There was, we had a management agreement, I believe,
with -- actually, management, not with IFA -- but there
is no direct relationship.
Q.  So the hotel management agreement that you referred to
is with respect to the Yotel project, I believe?
A.  Correct, well, Yotel The Palm, yes.
Q.  At what time is that agreement entered into?
A.  2015, I believe.
Q.  Okay.  Are you aware that around December 2017 IFA Yotel
Investments FZE, which I believe the entity with which
the hotel management agreement was, divested its
100 per cent investment in Yotel Investments Limited?
A.  What is the name of the first entity you mentioned,
sorry?
Q.  IFA Yotel Investment FZE, this is the UAE subsidary, I
believe, of IFA -- I mean of Yotel Investments Limited
or Yotel Limited.
A.  Of course I'm aware.
Q.  So you are saying that you are aware that
in December 2017 the UAE entity of the Yotel was
completely sold off?
A.  It was -- IFA Hotels and Resorts, through that vehicle
-- I didn't remember the name to be perfectly honest,
but that's the vehicle -- has divested from Yotel,
absolutely.
Q.  Okay.
A.  In fact, I think I mentioned it in my second statement.
It was part of a restructuring of our group.  So the
Yotel Investment Ltd vehicle, which used to be owned by
IFA Hotels and Resorts through various vehicles, was
spin off to the shareholders of IFA.
Q.  Okay.  Would you agree with me that Yotel was also
developing another hotel in Dubai with Dubai Investment
Properties with 565 keys?
A.  So we were not developing a hotel, but we were -- we had
a management agreement with Dubai Investment Properties
to operate a hotel on Sheikh Zayed road.  I think the
number of keys was 581, if I remember correctly, I'm not
100 per cent sure.  Around that, yes.
But to be clear, the developer was Dubai Investment
Properties, not Yotel.
Q.  I understood.  So basically it was a hotel management
agreement that Yotel had with Dubai Investment
Properties?
A.  Correct.
Q.  Do you still manage the hotel of Dubai --
A.  DIP.
Q.  -- investment properties?
A.  That hotel has never opened.
Q.  Okay.
A.  It has completed, but it has not opened.
Q.  I see.  So because of that you could not officially
start the hotel management --
A.  If you want a clear answer, the developer, DIP, has not
fulfilled its agreement, and therefore the HMA, the
hotel management agreement we had with them, was
terminated.  And as a result, the hotel has never
opened.
Q.  Is there any other hotels in UAE that is currently
managed by Yotel?
A.  Currently managed, no.
Q.  Going back to my earlier question, you have stated that,
yes, you were aware that by around end of December 2017
IFA Hotel Investments FZE, which is the entity that was
in UAE holding the Yotel brand, was divested and
therefore that entity ceased to operate?
A.  I don't know what happened to the entity, to be honest.
What I know is that they were not the shareholders of
Yotel afterwards.  But I believe it was in October
or November, not December.  The management agreement.
That's when we introduced a new investor in our company.
Q.  I see.
A.  Because there was a restructuring of Yotel, we had a new
investor coming in, Starwood Capital Group, and IFA's
parent company, or major shareholder, decided to pull
the investment into Yotel directly.
Q.  So what happened to the agreement that was entered in
2015 for the hotel management of Yotel The Palm?
A.  It is unrelated.  You mean today?
Q.  No, when the --
A.  Back in the day?
Q.  Yes.
A.  It was unrelated because it was between two different
entities, so the fact that our shareholders were
changing had no impact on the HMA we had directly with
the -- is it Balquis or ...?  I think the HMA would have
been with Balquis Residence.  Normally we send HMA
directly with the entity which owns the asset, not with
the parent company.  So that would have had no impact
whatsoever.  In fact, I can add to this, that back when
we restructured Yotel, on the shareholders of Yotel, and
Starwood Capital entered into our business, it was
a prerequisite to them that this hotel, Yotel The Palm,
would be developed.  One of the conditions that we would
develop this hotel.  So there was no change, as far as
Yotel is concerned, there was no change whatsoever.
Q.  So I understand that after terminating the contract with
the claimants, in January sometime, immediately another
consultant by the name NEB was appointed it curate the
design and to obtain NOC from Nakheel.  Are you aware of
that contract?
A.  This is not Yotel's responsibility.  As I mentioned
previously -- I mean in my witness statement, we were
not the developer of the project; we were the operator
and providing technical services to the developer,
Balquis Residence, to develop this hotel.  So that would
have been the responsibility of the developer, not
Yotel.
Q.  But --
A.  I really can't confirm that.
Q.  Okay.  Do you recall reviewing designs in 2018, early
2018, for submission for Nakheel?
A.  Personally?
Q.  Either you or your team members?
A.  It is possible.  To answer your question, do I recall,
no.  But it is possible.  We have continued to work on
this project for a while, so ... Personally, I don't
remember.  It is possible that someone in my team did.
Q.  Okay.  So the project would have been then proceeded in
A.  As far as Yotel is concerned, we had a valid management
contract, yes, so there was no -- it was a live project
as far as Yotel was concerned.
Q.  So do you have a project that is constructed in 2018
under the brand Yotel through which you are currently
exercising the hotel management service agreement?
A.  In Dubai you mean?
Q.  Yes?
A.  Not in Dubai, no.
ARBITRATOR:  Ms Bejoy, we have to go to the matters more.
Because there is a time issue here.
MS BEJOY:  Yes.  Thank you.
So Mr Hubert, I understand you had the opportunity
of reviewing the designs prepared by the claimants.
What was the major flaw in those designs, from a Yotel
expectation standards?
A.  I think the -- we had firstly the opportunity to review
what was presented, right, which are relatively
preliminary designs, they are layouts, okay, and
renderings of a facade and so forth, and general layouts
of the project, right.
As I mentioned, and in my witness statements, you
know, we have our team, which is totally normal, our
technical services team has participated in the
development of this design, to eventually meet, to
a certain extent, the expected standards, bearing in
mind that this project also had to meet the Dubai DTCM
standards.  It was not just about meeting the Yotel
standards.
So after several iterations, as is reasonably normal
in such project, we started to reach a point where the
preliminary concept design layouts seemed to be going in
the right direction.  Bearing in mind that there was
still a lot of work to be done.
Q.  Okay.
So when the project was relooked at through
a different consultant in 2018, whether those standards
were applicable?
A.  I can't recall that second round, so I'm not sure what
you are referring to, whatever was reviewed in 2018.
I would be very happy to let you know, but I --
Q.  Yes, I will produce -- can we look at {D67}.  Do you
recall seeing this document, Mr Hubert?
A.  Lead consultancy?  No.  I don't recall.  Not saying
I haven't, but I don't recall.
Q.  Yes, and if we go down to page {D67-8}, you can see
under small letter (u), there is a definition for "Yotel
Standards".  It reads:
"'Yotel Standards' means the Standards of the Hotel
Operator (Yotel) stated in Schedule 1 as may be amended
and/or modified by the Employer from time to time ..."
So I believe that the mere fact that the definition
is there in the consultancy agreement, the expectation
was that the design that was to be produced by NEB was
also to meet the standards of Yotel?
A.  Yes, of course.  As for any hotel.  We are putting our
hotel in a very specific brand which is very specific
requirements, so whoever is the developer, whoever is
the contractor, has got access to our standards.
Q.  But you don't recall reviewing any designs from NEB?
A.  Personally, I don't, no.  Frankly speaking.  It is quite
possible.  I mean, I don't review every project.  That's
why we have a team.
Q.  Yes, I understand.  But you were, you know, the
decision-maker for the UAE region, even in 2018, with
respect to projects?
A.  Yotel, you mean?
Q.  For the Yotel, yes.
A.  Yes, global even, you can say.  I was the CEO of the
company, so ...
Q.  Yes.  So if there was any project that was to be
implemented in 2018 under the Yotel brand, you would
know?
A.  Yes.  But it is not -- again, of course I was aware we
were doing a project in Dubai.  As I said, for us,
whatever happened -- it is not our business to, as
a brand and an operator to decide who builds what and so
forth, we just want to make sure that what is being
built is a Yotel, because that's our brand.
So yes, we were obviously quite aware in 2018 and
2019 and 2017 that we had a hotel development on The
Palm.
Q.  Yes.  Why I'm asking this question is because in 2018
I see that there is no IFA Yotel -- Hotel Investment
FZE.
A.  That's not our entity; that was our shareholder.
Q.  Okay.  So which --
A.  Our contract was between, if I remember correctly, and
if you want I can check, we had a subsidiary called
Yotel Dubai LLC or FZE, I think it was an FZE, which had
a management contract with Balquis.  The entity you are
referring to is our shareholders' entity.  So it would
not have been party to the HMA.
Q.  Okay.
A.  We usually hold our HMA through SPVs.
Q.  Can we look at document {D90-50}.  This is the annual
financial report of IFA for the year 2018.
A.  Mm-hmm.
Q.  If you look at the properties under development which is
item 21, the group's properties under development
consists of the following.
" - UAE (Balquis Residence, C Fourteen and KOS
Heritage Place)."
A.  Mm-hmm.
Q.  Is this KOS Heritage Place that which was previously
Yotel The Palm?
A.  I have no idea how these books were prepared.  I'm not
in charge of IFA.  It is possible, but what does it
actually refer to?  I invite you to ask the CFO of IFA.
I suppose it is possible.
Q.  Yes.  But you are not aware of, you know, the Yotel The
Palm being renamed as KOS Heritage Place in 2018?
A.  If anything, it would have been the previous name, if
that's actually what it is.
Q.  Okay.
A.  Because as I'm sure you are aware, there was a different
project before the Yotel.  And I'm pretty sure it was
called Heritage Place.  So it is quite likely, I can't
confirm, it is quite likely that it would be the
previous name of the project.  But I don't know what KOS
means.
Q.  Mr Hubert, I understand that initially you, along with
other team members, were reviewing the design submitted
by the claimants, and towards the end of December or
early January 2017 I could not find emails from the
Yotel team reviewing the design submitted by the
claimants.  Any potential reasons for that?
A.  Yeah, I can give you many.  Firstly, you have to
appreciate that the developer of this project, Balquis,
decided to develop this project on what is called the
design and build contract which, from our experience as
a hotel manager and operator, is a rather unusual way to
develop a hotel.  We usually develop full detailed
drawings and then we tender for a contractor to build.
We don't ask the contractor to design our hotels.
So it put us in a rather unusual situation to start
with, which was something we don't usually do is
speaking with the contractor.  It is very uncommon.
Usually we only speak to our developer and the developer
has to speak with the contractor.
But obviously since it was a design and build
contract, well, we had to, pardon my -- educate the
contractor as to what is a Yotel, and that's why you
would have seen a lot of involvement at the beginning of
the project directly with the contractor.
Thereafter, honestly, our role have probably
returned to what is normally the way we function, is we
speak to our client and our client is Balquis, it is not
the contractor or the consultant, whoever it is, we
speak to the developer directly.
And that's probably the reason why at this stage,
once that first initial plan was done, we will speak to
Balquis from now on.  Honestly, it is the developer's
decision how they want to do that.  It is not us.  But
there it is rather unusual, as I said, that we speak
directly to a contractor.
Q.  So you just referred to the unusual arrangement of
a developer coming in the capacity also as the
contractor doing a design and build contract.
What was your understanding about this arrangement?
Was it like a JV?
A.  No, I am not sure -- I mean, as I said, originally
I actually voiced my concern about such an arrangement,
it has got nothing to do with the specific contractor,
it is like, it is just -- hotels are such specific
designs that usually you develop full detailed drawings
before you go and appoint a contractor.
So -- but Balquis assured us that it could be done,
and I know it can be done, I was also a developer in the
past, I understand what design and build is, it is just
usually more utilised for residential projects or
a commercial project or office buildings, but for hotels
it is a bit more unusual, let's put it this way.
So I suppose there was a will from Balquis to work
on this basis, and I also suppose -- I'm not also deaf
or blind -- that the financial contribution that the
contractor was willing to do was attractive to the
developer, right?  And that's why we went on this basis.
Or IFA/Balquis decided to work on this basis, rather
than the more traditional tender process that we would
have normally seen for this kind of situation.
Q.  If I could please refer you to paragraph 12 of your
first witness statement, Mr Hubert, {C2-2}.
A.  Yes.
Q.  So as you can see you are referring to some structural
constraints that existed in that particular plot of
land?
A.  Yes.
Q.  Could you please elaborate on what was the structural
constraint in the plot?
A.  As far as I remember there were really two, very
specific.  I mean, constraints doesn't mean it's making
it impossible, it just has to be taken into
consideration.
As you previously referred to, you mentioned this
Heritage Place project, which as far as I remember was
the name of the project which was originally planned for
that site, which was a residential project.  Therefore,
it had significantly less keys than what we were
anticipating to do with the Yotel, and the -- what
I would call the constraint is that the piling for
a project had already been done, and it is very
difficult to remove piles from the ground.  You can, but
it's financially exhaustive.
So that was challenge number 1, so how do you deal
with this?  Because it means your basement has got piles
in locations you don't necessarily want them to be, so
it creates a constraint from a design point of view, and
it creates -- it is technical but it is -- and the
second one is on that site, and I think this is what
I mentioned, there is a water tank, it is quite large,
for the building next door, and you just can't remove
it.  So you have to design around that water tank,
right?
So, look, everything is possible in design, and with
good engineering, but obviously this had to be taken
into account for any project, including the Yotel.
Q.  Okay.
MS BEJOY:  Thank you, Mr Hubert, that's all from me.
MR LIXENBURG:  Nothing from me.
ARBITRATOR:  No questions?  I have several questions.
I hope I will be quick.
Questions from THE ARBITRATOR
ARBITRATOR:  During 2016 until 2018, beginning of 2018, what
was your position on the Yotel?  Was an employee of
Yotel?
A.  Absolutely.  CEO of Yotel.
ARBITRATOR:  During the period where the claimants were in
a contract with IFA subsidiaries, you were actively
involved with the contractor or with the designers,
correct?
A.  Yes.
ARBITRATOR:  From Yotel side?
A.  Yes, of course, yes.
ARBITRATOR:  What was the challenge, in your opinion, with
the contractor?  Or with the designers?
A.  I said the main challenge for us was conceptual, right,
as a brand, as a developer, as -- well, Yotel is the
brand, like selecting a design and build solution was,
we thought, very ambitious, to say the least.  Not that
Yotels are the most luxurious hotels in the world and so
forth, but still, it is far more complex than doing
a residential building.  So I think that was challenge
number 1.
And -- but this could have been said about our
contractor, but the specific contractor we had had no
previous experience with our brand, which is fair
enough, our brand was very new, right.  So there was a
whole part of educating who we are, what we do, how we
do our hotels and so forth, which would have been quite
challenging.
The approach to the design was -- there was a lot of
effort put into figuring out the facade of the building
and so forth, which are all very important, but in my
opinion, can come much later in a project.  What is very
important is just figuring out the gross floor area, the
layouts of the floors, et cetera, which was eventually
done, but a lot of time was also spent on the look and
feel of the building.  It may have been a Nakheel
requirement, I don't know, but it is unusual for a hotel
project at such an early stage -- this is very early
days, right -- to be focusing on the look and feel of
the building.
ARBITRATOR:  Have you seen the initial concept design which
has been produced by the claimants here?
A.  Yes, there has been a couple of iterations, at least,
yes.
ARBITRATOR:  What is your opinion about that?  What is the
challenge on that?
A.  The one that we have here?  The one which was submitted
to -- is that the one you are referring to?
ARBITRATOR:  Not the one which is -- I'm talking about the
initial design which is the claimants, the concept
design, let's put it this way.
A.  Do you happen to have it?  I remember this one vividly,
obviously.
ARBITRATOR:  Which one are you referring to?
A.  That's the one which was submitted to Nakheel,
I believe.
MR LIXENBURG:  Is there a reference, because Mr Viriot has
a hard copy, so maybe --
A.  I don't know who is controlling it.
ARBITRATOR:  Can somebody help us and put it on the screen?
MR LIXENBURG:  Is there a number at the bottom of the page?
A.  Here it is number 8, and on the paper -- I'm still on my
witness statement here.
MS BEJOY:  {D10}.
ARBITRATOR:  Can you put it up, please, on the screen.
Have you seen this before?
A.  Yes.
ARBITRATOR:  What was your opinion from Yotel point of view?
A.  From a Yotel, if you compare --
ARBITRATOR:  Because you are representing the Yotel.
A.  Sure, sure.
ARBITRATOR:  Okay.
A.  It is a very highly spec-ed building compared to do what
we usually do.  With some elements which, you know, we
thought were probably very nice to have, but not
necessarily necessary.  Generally speaking, we
participate -- my team, even myself participated quite
a bit on this, so by the time we got to this stage,
I think we were quite happy with the room layouts and
how they worked and the room mix.  By that time
I think -- I don't see the date here, but I think we
would have reached the requirements of the DTCM in terms
of the number of standard rooms, number of suites,
number of ADA rooms, et cetera.  So by then we are, you
know, in the core of it in terms of general layout.
Insofar as having atriums and lifts facing the beach
and all that, I mean these are not brand standards,
these is like going above.
When you are sitting as a brand, if you have an
owner who is willing to spend more, maybe it is okay,
but it is unusual.  Usually it is the other way around,
they want to cut.
ARBITRATOR:  Right.  You were aware when the respondents
terminated their contract?
A.  (Shakes head).
ARBITRATOR:  Did they inform you?
A.  I don't recall, no, honestly.  I don't recall being --
and they didn't have to.  But --
ARBITRATOR:  I'm sure it is not -- because it is their
relationship.  But because you were involving --
A.  I don't recall it being formally informed or not.  Could
they have told me over the phone, it is possible.
ARBITRATOR:  You don't recall -- not formally, I'm not
talking about formally, just knowledge.
A.  I don't -- I'm not sure.
ARBITRATOR:  That's fine.  Is the agreement between Yotel
and IFA subsidiary has been terminated?  Or --
A.  The management agreement?
ARBITRATOR:  Yes.
A.  It was later terminated, yes.
ARBITRATOR:  Which year?
A.  Much later.
ARBITRATOR:  You don't recall?
A.  2020, after COVID, I think, or during COVID.  21, 22.
ARBITRATOR:  2021 or 2022, okay.
A.  Yes.  Because as I said earlier, we as the company had a
commitment vis a vis one of our shareholders to deliver
this hotel.  So when that was terminated, needless to
say it caused trouble for Yotel.
ARBITRATOR:  Sure.  Have you involved actively -- okay,
I will just rephrase it.  Have you involved on the
design after, on 2018 onwards?
A.  I don't recall, no.  Generally speaking, I'm quite
passionate about development, therefore at the beginning
of project I'm quite involved, and then as we go more
into normal construction and growth, my technical
services team just does the job, and I get back involved
towards the end.  Which would be the normal case there.
So secondly, there is a slight difference, when we
started this project, when we signed in 15, I think, our
management contract -- and to be perfectly honest Yotel
was a very small company back then, and by the time we
are now in 2020 and so forth, and we were delivering
many hotels, so I also had to change my involvement into
projects to be a bit more restrained to avoid delays and
so forth.  But yes, I would have been -- as I think it
was established, more involved at the beginning, and
towards 18 I would have been much less involved.
ARBITRATOR:  Much less, that means you was involved also?
A.  No, it means like, well, my technical services team
would probably report to me -- well, they would report
to me and let me know, we would have a regular review of
what is happening with the project, right.  But they're
going into the details of, you know ...
ARBITRATOR:  Okay.  Have your team keep reporting you about
the changing of new consultants?
A.  No.  It is highly possible, but I can't recall,
honestly.
ARBITRATOR:  Thank you very much.  I have no more questions.
MR LIXENBURG:  May I just ask one question arising from your
own questions?
ARBITRATOR:  Please, go ahead.
Further examination by MR LIXENBURG
MR LIXENBURG:  The arbitrator was asking you about the
design and your view on the design produced by the
claimants.  Could you just explain to the arbitrator
what your view of the design was from the perspective of
the progress and stage of the design?
A.  So I think, as was established, we started from scratch
a project on a complicated site, complicated in the
sense it has constraints, as discussed.
We got to that stage, I think that's probably the
last iteration, which -- I mean, I think forget the
picture, if you look at the plan, we had layout.  Layout
is good, but it is the very beginning of a long process,
right.
So thereafter you are supposed to develop 3D designs
and MEP designs and coordinate all the different designs
and so forth, so we were very far off from there.  What
we had was the initial layout on the basis of which we
could say, okay, the rooms are the size we need, the mix
is the mix we want, and generally speaking the layout in
terms of -- is workable for our brand.  So that's a good
initial stage, but from that point onwards normally
there is a huge amount of work to be done, and I think
that's where it got stuck, so we have never really got
to that stage.
MR LIXENBURG:  Thank you very much.
ARBITRATOR:  Thank you for your time.
WITNESS:  Thank you very much for accommodating an early
meeting.
ARBITRATOR:  Wish you a safe journey.  You are free to
leave.
(The witness was released)
ARBITRATOR:  Anybody want to take a coffee?  Or you want to
continue?  For me I'm fine.
MR LIXENBURG:  Happy to carry on.  I will just show
Mr Viriot out.
MR KHALED ESBAITAH (previously called)
Cross-examination by MS BEJOY (continued)
ARBITRATOR:  Before we start, how long we need?  30 minutes
you have?
MS BEJOY:  I may not take 30, but just to --
ARBITRATOR:  Maximum 30.
MS BEJOY:  Yes.
ARBITRATOR:  Go direct to your questions, please.
MS BEJOY:  Thank you.
ARBITRATOR:  Good morning.
A.  Good morning.
MS BEJOY:  Good morning, Mr Khaled.
ARBITRATOR:  Hope you had a good night, peacefully, nobody
bothered you.
A.  Thank you, sir.
ARBITRATOR:  We continue only your witness statement today.
A.  Okay.
